newsitem.title: GERMANY: Iranian to testify in camera in Berlin murder case.
newsitem.headline: Iranian to testify in camera in Berlin murder case.

text.p: A Berlin court said on Tuesday it would bar the public and media to protect an Iranian witness in the trial of five men suspected of carrying out political assassinations on Tehran's orders.
Judge Frithjof Kubsch said the man, a former Iranian government official who fled after being sentenced to death and who has not been named for his own safety, would take the stand on Thursday.
The witness's name was put forward by the prosecution's star witness, exiled former Iranian president Abolhassan Banisadr.
Banisadr told the court in August that Iran's religious leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei ordered the killings and President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani signed the order.
Banisadr cited the defector as one of his sources and prosecutors say his inside knowledge means his life would be in danger if he were identified.

The court has spent almost three years hearing evidence in the trial of four Lebanese and an Iranian on suspicion of shooting dead three exiled Iranian Kurdish leaders and their translator in Berlin's Mykonos restaurant in September 1992.

The case prompted the German justice authorities to issue an arrest warrant for Iranian Intelligence Minister Ali Fallahiyan in March, straining relations between Bonn and Iran, which denies any involvement.
